newsitem.title: UK: UK spot natgas up in June, barely traded further o.
newsitem.headline: UK spot natgas up in June, barely traded further o.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market was stronger in June on Thursday, traders and brokers said, but further out trade was barely seen as many in the market disappeared to Headingley to watch the first one day cricket international between England and Australia.

"There's quite a lot of buying interest for June," said a trader. He added that there were plentiful bids and offers, and that interest was picking up "which is what you often find when a month goes prompt."
Another trader said he thought some of the interest in June may have been explained by "someone picking it up cheap in the last few days and selling it on now."

Beyond June, there was an interesting third quarter deal reported for 300,000 th/d, 12 times larger than the current standard size of a deal for a full quarter. The trade was done at a discount to two indices, with a floor price agreed at an absolute level to protect the seller if the price collapses.
"If the index comes in below the floor, then the floor prevails," explained one of the counterparties to the trade.
The trader added that this type of deal appears to be gaining in popularity, although "I think people who want to sell on that basis may have difficulty in finding a buyer."

With the exception of June, prices were unchanged in the absence of any real activity. With many absent watching cricket in Leeds, some of the remaining London-based traders took advantage of the quiet conditions to enjoy long lunches, and little of substance was done.
The IPE was another victim of the cricket, with no trade done at all and hardly any bids or offers posted by the close.
